name: claude-code-self-tools
description: Small Claude Code plugins that let a session act on itself: compact or clear its conversation, reload its plugins, reconnect an MCP server, read its context window, check its own tools, wake itself later, turn on Remote Control under a title, exit or restart, and switch to another conversation. Install only the ones you want.

plugins.name: self-compact
plugins.description: Compacts the conversation once the turn ends, at the break between two pieces of work, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-clear
plugins.description: Clears the conversation once the turn ends, only when its work is complete or its context is contaminated, and starts the next piece from a handoff it writes.

plugins.name: self-reload
plugins.description: Reloads the session's plugins once the turn ends, as /reload-plugins does, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-mcp
plugins.description: Reconnects an MCP server that broke (one by name, or all) once the turn ends, as /mcp reconnect does, then resumes on its own.

plugins.name: self-context
plugins.description: Reads how full the context window is, and whether auto-compact is on, to decide whether to compact at a break.

plugins.name: self-check
plugins.description: Checks that the session's own tools answer: a nonce echoed through Bash and PowerShell as the model calls them, the room the session env leaves a Bash command, and the MCP servers listed (exercised only through probes you name). Quietly again at resume, saying only what failed. Dedupes Bash's session env after each session start, against Git Bash's 8,186-character cut.

plugins.name: self-wake
plugins.description: Wakes the session some minutes after the turn ends with a note it sends itself, to check back on slow work.

plugins.name: self-remote-control
plugins.description: Reports on the session's Remote Control, connects it under a title, and renames the session. After a login change it reconnects Remote Control and resumes a turn the change cut off. It runs /remote-control only while the session is not connected.

plugins.name: self-exit
plugins.description: Ends the session once the turn ends, as /exit does, with a stated reason recorded in its transcript for whoever resumes it; it refuses while a session cron, a background job or a subagent would make /exit ask, saying how to stop each.

plugins.name: self-restart
plugins.description: Restarts the session on Windows once the turn ends: a new window, or the pane's slot, resumes the same conversation once the old process has exited, then resumes work on its own.

plugins.name: self-switch
plugins.description: Switches the terminal to another conversation on Windows once the turn ends, for your own use: only when that conversation is open nowhere on this machine and nothing runs under this session; in place, in the pane's slot, or in a new window. It refuses where the coordinator runs switches.
